native_result.query: In which millenium did amber had the highest value and in what time interval did it peak?
native_result.HypoA: Amber has historically high and stable values in the 4th millenium BCE. with its all time peak around 3300 to 3000BCE.
native_result.HypoB: Amber had its highest value in the 4th millennium BCE (4000–3001 BCE; no-year-zero convention). Within that millennium its standardized z-score attains an absolute maximum of +1.54 across a contiguous plateau of four 100-year bins with start years 3300, 3200, 3100, and 3000 BCE, giving a peak time interval of 3300–3001 BCE at the very end of the 4th millennium BCE. This conclusion is independent of source: Zamber in data/capital.csv (the discrete per-period z-score, 100-yr bins, 500–4300 BCE) and Amber / Amber_inter in data/time_series_data.csv (the same series plus its 1-year linear interpolation over CE −4100 to −500 / calBP 2450–6050) both reach z = 1.54 at the same four 100-year-bin start years (CE −3300, −3200, −3100, −3000). Per-millennium mean Zamber in the 4th millennium BCE is 1.484 (10 bins), versus −0.148 in the 3rd, −0.576 in the 2nd, −0.727 in the 1st BCE, and −1.07 in the 5th (only the 4000 BCE bin falls in the data's 4300→500 BCE range). The third supplied file, pollen_openness_score_Belau_Woserin_Feeser_et_al_2019.csv, contains only pollen-PCA columns and no amber data, so it is not relevant to this question.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/capital.csv, data/time_series_data.csv, and data/pollen_openness_score_Belau_Woserin_Feeser_et_al_2019.csv; cleaned comma-decimal locale in capital.csv (and the pollen file) to floats; verified that Zamber in capital.csv (39 rows, BCE 4300→500 in 100-yr steps, all six archaeological periods EN/MN/SG/LN/OBA/YBA covered) is the same discrete series as Amber (raw) in time_series_data.csv (3601 rows, CE −4100→−500 in 1-yr steps), and that Amber_inter is its dense 1-year linear interpolation (cross-source max consistent at 1.54, plateau bins identical). Computed per-millennium aggregates using the no-year-zero convention (Nth mill. BCE = [N·1000, (N−1)·1000 + 1] BCE). Identified the global peak Zamber = +1.54 in four contiguous 100-year bins starting at 3300/3200/3100/3000 BCE; the 4th millennium BCE has the highest mean and ties for the highest max, so it is the millennium with the highest amber value, and the peak time interval is 3300–3001 BCE. Excluded the pollen_openness_score file (no amber columns). The full analysis script and JSON report are saved under /workspace/analysis/.
